operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole clause transfers the functions, powers and duties of the High Commissioner, with the personnel, records, property and funds of the office, to the Secretary of the Interior. Paragraph 1 of EO 9616, signed September 14, 1945 (10 FR 11837), repeals EO 9245 by number and date and transfers the same matters back to the High Commissioner; the held Federal Register text shows no deferred effective date, so the first end is 1945-09-14 by presidential express repeal.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and statutes of the 
United States, particularly the First War 
Powers Act, 1941 (Public Law 354—77th 
Congress), it is hereby ordered that the 
functions, powers, and duties of the 
United States High Commissioner to the 
Philippine Islands, together with the per­
sonnel, records, property, and funds of 
the office of the High Commissioner, be, 
and they are hereby, transferred to the 
Secretary of the Interior.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 20 of the Rubber Producing

App. 1941r), and by section 6 (d) of the 
act of March 21, 1956, 70 Stat. 53, and 
as President of the United States, it is 
ordered as follows:
Section  1. Subject to the provisions 
of section 2 of this order, the Federal 
Facilities Corporation (hereinafter re­
ferred to as the Corporation) is hereby 
designated as the agency to administer 
the contracts of sale or lease of the 
Government-owned rubber producing fa­
cilities made pursuant to the Rubber 
Producing Facilities Disposal Act of 1953, 
as amended, and to administer other 
matters involving the Rubber Producing 
Facilities Disposal Commission, includ­
ing all powers and authority conferred

5 , and 6  of the said act of March 21,1956, 
and also including the winding up of the 
affairs of the Commission. The said con­
tracts are hereby transferred to the Cor­
poration.

national-security clause contained in

contained in any lease of the unsold fa­

Secretary of Defense.

research_rationale:
EO 10679 (21 FR 7199, September 20, 1956; held official Federal Register text) prescribed regulations for agreements between the Secretary of Defense and the States on withholding State retirement contributions from the pay of civilian Army and Air National Guard employees under the act of June 15, 1956. Section 8 of EO 10996 of February 16, 1962 states "This order supersedes Executive Order No. 10679 of" September 20, 1956, and restates each of its commands in sections 1 to 6 of EO 10996 with the 1961 amendments. Every clause therefore ended on 1962-02-16 and the order was not in force on 2026-10-14. The machine inventory is corrected: paragraph 1 was one 12,448-character clause that swallowed a page break and unrelated contents pages, so it is split into its two real fragments. The U.S. Code note at 5 U.S.C. 5518 prints EO 10996 including its section 8, which agrees.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Searched the held texts citing EO 10679 by number: only EO 10996 (Federal Register text and APP transcription) is a later instrument; the other hits are the order's own text. The order has no sunset or condition, and its 120-day time limit applies to each State request, not to the order. No amendment, partial revocation or earlier supersession is held, so nothing precedes 1962-02-16.","independent_command_check":"Individual agreements already made between the Secretary of Defense and a State under EO 10679 are separate instruments; section 7 of EO 10996 keeps them in force until amended, modified or terminated. They are not commands of EO 10679 and do not keep any clause of this order operative, so they are treated as savings, not as an independent command.","savings_check":"Section 7 of EO 10996 continues determinations, regulations, agreements and other actions taken with respect to a function affected by EO 10996 and not revoked, superseded or made inapplicable before its date, except to the extent inconsistent with it. Agreements made under EO 10679 therefore continue as agreements, but EO 10679 itself is superseded; the continuing instruments are independent of this order.","scope_check":"Section 8 of EO 10996 supersedes EO 10679 as a whole by number and date. Each of the eight corrected clauses has a counterpart in EO 10996 sections 1 to 6, which is why the whole order, not part of it, is superseded; the authority to prescribe rules in paragraph 6 is re-delegated in section 6 of EO 10996."}

THE PRESIDENT 4323
Executive Order 11962 January 19, 1977
Establishing the President’s Advisory Board on International Investment
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and statutes of the 
United States of America, including section 8(a) of the International Investment 
Survey Act of 1976 (90 Stat. 2064, 22 U.S.C. 3107), and as President of the United 
States of America, in accordance with the provisions of the Federal Advisory Commit­
tee Act (5 U.S.C. App. I ) , it is hereby ordered as follows:
S e c t i o n 1. (a) There is hereby established the President’s Advisory Board on In­
ternational Investment, hereinafter referred to as the Board, which shall be composed 
of not more than fifteen members who shall be appointed by the President. Each 
member shall serve for a term limited to the remaining life of the Board as determined 
at the time of appointment.
(b) The President shall designate a Chairman and Vice Chairman from among ' 
the members.
Sec. 2. (a) Whenever requested, the Board shall advise the Executive Director 
of the Council on International Economic Policy, hereinafter referred to as the Execu­
tive Director, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, and the heads 
of other agencies, with respect to matters relating to the performance of their func­
tions under the International Investment Survey Act of 1976 (90 Stat. 2059, 22 
U.S.C. 3101) .
(b) In making its recommendations, the Board1  shall give due consideration to 
the usefulness of data to be collected as compared to the burden imposed on those who 
are to furnish the data.
Sec. 3. (a) The Executive Director shall, to the extent permitted by law, provide 
administrative and staff services, support, and facilities for the Board.
(b) The Executive Director shall appoint an Executive Secretary for the Board.
Sec. 4. Members of the Board may be compensated for their services in accord  
with 5 U.S.C. 3109, and may, to the extent permitted by law, be allowed travel ex­
penses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, as authorized by law (5 U.S.C. 5702 
and 5703) for persons in the government service employed intermittently.
Sec. 5. Notwithstanding the provisions o fy any other Executive order, the func­
tions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App. I ) , 
except that of reporting annually to the Congress, which are applicable to the Board, 
shall be performed by the Executive Director in accordance with guidelines and proce­
dures established by the Office of Management and Budget.
Sec. 6. The Board shall terminate on December 3 1 -, 1978, unless sooner extended.
T h e W h i t e H o u s e,
January 19, 1977.
